page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 12 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 10% to 25% tier. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the Geekbench multi-core score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth remains stable at average levels, reaching 59.2 GB/sec for large-block reads, though the overall Passmark memory score is positioned in the lower 25%. Database operations and Redis SET performance also align with mid-range expectations, achieving 8.48 million operations per second in Redis testing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge offers a favorable profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency single-core compute. By providing 96 GB of RAM alongside 12 vCPUs, it allows organizations to host memory-bound applications without paying for unnecessary CPU cores. This makes the instance suitable for database hosting, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded data processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint.
